title: Attackers Exploit Optimizely Flaw To Inject Malicious JavaScript
content_md: IntroductionOn November 16, 2026, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation account signup flow. Optimizely is a platform used to create, manage, test, and personalize digital content and websites. The flaw allowed the attacker to edit the Project JavaScript (projectJS) field. Customers use this field to add custom code that runs on pages that load the Optimizely snippet. By abusing this mechanism, the attacker injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects. The code was then delivered to visitors’ browsers through the Optimizely snippets, including snippets served from Optimizely’s content delivery network (CDN).The attack highlights the continued risk posed by third-party script dependencies and software supply chain compromises, particularly when websites rely on trusted third-party platforms to deliver JavaScript that runs in visitors’ browsers.Optimizely reported that it blocked the vulnerable path, deployed a fix, removed the injected code from affected projects, ended active sessions, revoked tokens, reset access for affected accounts, and notified impacted customers.The malicious payload was designed to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skim payment card details, steal cookies, capture page screenshots, and deliver iOS exploits to iPhones and iPads.
